title: Reference Type vs Actual Object Type
summary: Compile-time view vs runtime execution reality.

activities.title: Everyday Analogy: The Universal Remote Control
activities.concept: Reference Type (Compile-Time Lens) vs Actual Object Type (Runtime Reality)

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: Imagine you have a universal television remote control labeled 'Basic TV Remote' that only has Power, Volume, and Channel buttons. You point it at an ultra-modern 8K Smart OLED TV capable of 3D gaming, voice streaming, and ambient lighting. Because your remote only has basic buttons, you can only press Volume and Channel through that remote. However, when you press 'Power On', the screen doesn't turn on like an old CRT; it fires up its advanced 8K OLED processor and displays HDR visuals!
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: In Java, the reference variable is the 'remote control' (reference type), and the object in the Heap is the 'actual device' (runtime object type). The reference type dictates which methods you are allowed to call at compile-time (the remote's physical buttons). But the actual object type dictates HOW those methods execute at runtime (the TV's true hardware response).
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: Compile time looks at the reference type to verify method existence; runtime looks at the actual object type on the heap to execute the overridden implementation.

activities.title: The Duality of Java References
activities.content:
### Two Worlds: Compile Time vs Runtime

Every object reference in Java exists in two distinct phases:

1. **Compile-Time Reference Type (The View)**:
   - This is the type declared on the left side of the assignment: `Vehicle v = new SportsCar();`
   - The compiler uses `v`'s declared type (`Vehicle`) as a strict filter. You can **only** call methods that exist in `Vehicle`.
   - If `SportsCar` has an exclusive method `turboBoost()`, calling `v.turboBoost()` results in a compile-time error: `cannot find symbol method turboBoost()`.

2. **Runtime Actual Object Type (The Heap Instance)**:
   - This is the concrete class instantiated with `new` on the right side: `new SportsCar()`.
   - When a valid method (like `v.start()`) is invoked, the Java Virtual Machine uses **dynamic method dispatch** to execute the version defined in `SportsCar`, not `Vehicle`.

### The Fundamental Rule of Method Resolution
> **Method Accessibility is determined by the Reference Type; Method Execution is determined by the Actual Object Type.**

```
Reference Type (Vehicle)  --------> Decides WHAT can be called (Compile-Time Check)
Actual Object (SportsCar) --------> Decides WHICH code executes (Runtime Dispatch)
```

### Memory Visualization
- **Stack Frame**: Holds the reference variable `v` (4 or 8 bytes containing a 64-bit memory address).
- **Heap Space**: Holds the full `SportsCar` instance with all its fields, its virtual method table (`vtable`) pointer, and header metadata.

activities.title: Demonstrating Reference Type Restrictions and Dynamic Dispatch
activities.explanation: Even though the heap holds a SportsCar, variable v is typed as Vehicle. Thus, the compiler only permits calling methods declared on Vehicle. But when start() is called, SportsCar's override runs.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `SportsCar` overrides `start()` and adds a new method `turboBoost()`.
`Vehicle v = new SportsCar();` stores a SportsCar in a Vehicle reference.
`v.start()` passes compiler validation (Vehicle has `start()`) and dispatches to SportsCar's method at runtime.

activities.title: Heterogeneous Processing via Superclass Reference
activities.explanation: An array of the superclass reference type can hold any subclass instance. The loop calls send() polymorphically without knowing concrete types.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: Index 0 holds an `EmailNotification`; Index 1 holds an `SmsNotification`.
The loop invokes `n.send()`; the JVM checks each object's actual class in heap memory and calls the proper implementation.

activities.title: Reference Type vs Actual Object Type Quiz

questions.question: Given `Animal a = new Dog();`, what is the reference type and actual object type?
options: Reference type is Animal; Actual object type is Dog
Reference type is Dog; Actual object type is Animal
Both reference and actual object types are Animal
Both reference and actual object types are Dog
questions.explanation: The reference type is declared on the left (Animal); the actual instantiated object type is on the right with `new` (Dog).

questions.question: What decides which methods you are allowed to call on an object variable at compile time?
options: The declared reference type of the variable
The return type of the enclosing method
questions.explanation: The Java compiler strictly inspects the declared reference type to ensure invoked methods exist on that class or interface.

questions.question: If `Dog` has a method `bark()`, but `Animal` does NOT declare `bark()`, what happens if you execute `Animal a = new Dog(); a.bark();`?
options: It produces a compile-time compiler error
The JVM dynamically injects bark into Animal
questions.explanation: Because `Animal` does not define `bark()`, the compiler rejects the call before any bytecode is generated.

questions.question: Which mechanism enables Java to call the subclass's overridden method when invoked through a superclass reference?
questions.explanation: Dynamic method dispatch looks up the object's virtual method table (vtable) at runtime to invoke the actual overridden method.

questions.question: Where does the reference variable live, and where does the actual object live in memory?
options: Reference variable is on the Heap; object is on the Stack
Reference variable is on the Stack (or inside enclosing object); actual object is in the Heap
Both reside solely in the CPU L1 cache
Both reside in the PermGen space
questions.explanation: Local reference variables are stored in stack frames, whereas instantiated objects reside in heap memory.

questions.question: Can an interface be used as a reference type in Java?
options: No, only concrete classes can be reference types
No, only abstract classes can be reference types
Yes, any interface can serve as a reference type for classes that implement it
Yes, but only if the interface has zero methods
questions.explanation: Interfaces are widely used as reference types (e.g. `List<String> list = new ArrayList<>()`), encouraging programming to interfaces.

questions.question: Given `Object obj = "LearnBySelf";`, which of the following is legal without casting?
questions.explanation: `toString()` is defined on `java.lang.Object`, so the compiler permits it. `toUpperCase()`, `substring()`, and `charAt()` require a `String` reference or casting.

questions.question: Why is programming to a superclass or interface reference type considered a best practice?
options: It decouples code from concrete implementations, allowing future replacement with zero client code changes
questions.explanation: Coding to abstractions (e.g., `List` instead of `ArrayList`) maximizes modularity and loose coupling.

questions.question: What is the size of an object reference variable in 64-bit Java with Compressed OOPs enabled?
questions.explanation: Under 64-bit JVMs with Compressed OOPs (ordinary object pointers) active (heaps < 32GB), references take 4 bytes.

questions.question: If `class Cat extends Animal`, can you write `Cat c = new Animal();`?
options: Yes, but only if Cat has no extra methods
No, it results in a compile-time type mismatch error
questions.explanation: You cannot assign a general parent object to a specialized child reference; an Animal is not necessarily a Cat.

activities.title: Reference Type vs Actual Object Type Interview Questions

interviewQA.question: Explain the difference between compile-time type and runtime type of an object in Java.
interviewQA.answer: The compile-time type (static type) is the declared type of the reference variable. The compiler verifies method calls, access privileges, and assignments against this type. The runtime type (dynamic type) is the exact class instantiated on the heap with 'new'. The JVM uses the runtime type for dynamic method dispatch when invoking overridden instance methods.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Compile-time type determines what operations are permissible by the compiler. Runtime type determines which overridden method implementation executes in the JVM.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Reference type = compile-time gatekeeper; Actual type = runtime execution logic.
keyPoints: Reference type = compile-time gatekeeper; Actual type = runtime execution logic.

interviewQA.question: Why does `List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();` compile, but calling a method unique to `ArrayList` fail on `list`?
interviewQA.answer: Because `list` is declared with reference type `List<String>`, the compiler only allows methods declared in the `List` interface. Even though the underlying heap object is an `ArrayList`, methods specific to `ArrayList` (like `trimToSize()`) are invisible to the compiler through the `List` lens.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: The compiler checks method validity strictly against the reference type 'List', where implementation-specific methods do not exist.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Program to the interface to prevent leaking implementation details to callers.
keyPoints: Program to the interface to prevent leaking implementation details to callers.

interviewQA.question: What is the virtual method table (vtable) and how does it relate to runtime object types?
interviewQA.answer: The vtable is an internal JVM data structure associated with each loaded class containing pointers to the executable code of its instance methods. When `v.method()` is invoked, the JVM dereferences the object header in the heap to locate its class vtable and jumps to the concrete method implementation.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: A vtable contains pointers to method implementations. The JVM inspects the heap object's class vtable to execute dynamic dispatch.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Virtual method tables power dynamic dispatch at runtime.
keyPoints: Virtual method tables power dynamic dispatch at runtime.

interviewQA.question: Can static methods be dynamically dispatched based on the actual object type?
interviewQA.answer: No. Static methods belong to the class, not the instance. They are resolved at compile time using static binding based solely on the declared reference type. Subclassing a static method merely hides it, rather than overriding it.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Static methods are resolved at compile time based on reference type; they are never polymorphic.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Polymorphism and dynamic dispatch only apply to non-private, non-static instance methods.
keyPoints: Polymorphism and dynamic dispatch only apply to non-private, non-static instance methods.

interviewQA.question: What happens if a class extends a class and overrides a method with a covariant return type?
interviewQA.answer: Java allows an overriding method to declare a return type that is a subclass of the return type declared in the superclass (covariant return type). While the reference type determines the return type seen at compile time, the actual object returns the subtype at runtime.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Covariant return types allow subclasses to narrow the returned type while upholding the superclass contract.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Overridden methods may narrow return types safely.
keyPoints: Overridden methods may narrow return types safely.

interviewQA.question: How does `final` on a class or method impact the relationship between reference type and object type?
interviewQA.answer: A `final` method cannot be overridden, which allows the JVM/JIT compiler to perform devirtualization and inline the method call directly, eliminating vtable lookup overhead. A `final` class cannot be extended, meaning reference type and actual object type will always be identical.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Marking methods or classes final eliminates dynamic dispatch overhead via JIT inlining.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Final prevents polymorphic specialization and enables performance inlining.
keyPoints: Final prevents polymorphic specialization and enables performance inlining.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I can clearly distinguish between declared reference type and runtime object type.
I understand that the compiler uses the reference type to check method existence.
I understand that the JVM uses the actual object type for dynamic method dispatch.
I know why calling subclass-only methods through a superclass reference causes a compile error.
I can explain why static methods are resolved by reference type and not object type.
I can trace where references live (stack/heap) versus where instantiated objects live (heap).
I understand how polymorphic arrays (`Super[] arr`) handle heterogeneous child objects.
I know why 'programming to an interface' produces more maintainable code.
I can describe the role of the virtual method table (vtable) in method resolution.
I can predict the exact output of code combining inheritance and reference polymorphism.

practiceProblems.title: Warmup: Payment Gateway Reference View
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Complete the payment gateway demo:
1. Base class `Payment` with method `public void process(double amount)` printing `'Processing generic payment of $' + amount`.
2. Subclass `CreditCardPayment` extending `Payment`: overrides `process(double amount)` printing `'Charging credit card: $' + amount`.
3. In `main`, declare a reference variable of type `Payment` and instantiate it with `new CreditCardPayment()`. Call `process(150.0)`.
Observe that the method prints the credit card specific message.
hints: Declare `Payment p = new CreditCardPayment();` in main.

practiceProblems.title: Polymorphic Media Player Stream
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a media player hierarchy from scratch without starter code:
1. Base class `MediaItem` with a protected string `title`. Constructor takes `title`. Defines method `public void play()` printing `'Playing media: ' + title`.
2. Subclass `AudioTrack` extending `MediaItem`: constructor takes `(title, bitrate)`. Overrides `play()` printing `'Playing audio track: ' + title + ' @ ' + bitrate + 'kbps'`.
3. Subclass `VideoTrack` extending `MediaItem`: constructor takes `(title, resolution)`. Overrides `play()` printing `'Streaming video: ' + title + ' in ' + resolution`.
4. In `Main`, create an array `MediaItem[] playlist` containing an `AudioTrack("Podcast Ep 1", 320)` and a `VideoTrack("Nature Doc", "4K UHD")`.
5. Iterate through `playlist` invoking `play()` on each item.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Playing audio track: Podcast Ep 1 @ 320kbps
Streaming video: Nature Doc in 4K UHD
hints: Constructor chaining with super(title) is required in both subclasses.
Iterate over MediaItem[] using an enhanced for-loop.

practiceProblems.title: Cloud Resource Metric Collector
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Implement an extensible cloud resource metric collector from scratch without starter code:
1. Interface `CloudResource` with `String getId()` and `double getUtilization()`.
2. Class `ComputeInstance` implementing `CloudResource`: fields `id` (String) and `cpuPercent` (double). Implements interface methods accordingly.
3. Class `StorageBucket` implementing `CloudResource`: fields `id` (String), `usedGb` (double), `totalGb` (double). `getUtilization()` returns `(usedGb / totalGb) * 100.0`.
4. Class `ClusterMonitor` with static method `public static void printReport(CloudResource resource)` that prints `'Resource [' + resource.getId() + '] Utilization: ' + resource.getUtilization() + '%' `.
5. In `Main`, instantiate a `ComputeInstance("vm-web-01", 78.5)` and a `StorageBucket("s3-assets", 400.0, 1000.0)` as `CloudResource` references and pass each to `ClusterMonitor.printReport()`.
hints: CloudResource interface acts as the polymorphic parameter type in printReport.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Subclass-Only Method Call on Parent Reference
practiceProblems.problemStatement: A developer wrote the following code attempting to call a specialized subclass method `reboot()` through a superclass reference variable `Server s`, causing a compilation error. Fix the code by declaring `Server` appropriately or adjusting the method so the code compiles and outputs `'Rebooting node node-42'`.
hints: To call s.reboot() through reference type Server, reboot() must be declared in Server.
Subclass DatabaseServer overrides reboot() to provide its specialized implementation.

practiceProblems.title: Advanced: Dynamic Dispatch with Covariant Clone
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a prototype cloner demonstrating covariant returns from scratch without starter code:
1. Base class `Document` with protected `String content`. Constructor `Document(String content)`. Method `public Document copy()` that returns `new Document(this.content)`. Method `public void display()` printing `'Document: ' + content`.
2. Subclass `Spreadsheet` extending `Document`: constructor takes `content`. Overrides `copy()` with covariant return type `public Spreadsheet copy()` returning `new Spreadsheet(this.content + ' [GRID]')`. Overrides `display()` printing `'Spreadsheet: ' + content`.
3. In `Main`, create a `Document docRef = new Spreadsheet("Q3 Revenue")`.
4. Call `Document duplicate = docRef.copy();`.
5. Call `duplicate.display();`.
Verify that dynamic dispatch runs `Spreadsheet.copy()` and outputs `'Spreadsheet: Q3 Revenue [GRID]'`.
hints: In Spreadsheet, public Spreadsheet copy() is a legal covariant override of public Document copy().
When called through docRef, dynamic dispatch executes Spreadsheet's copy method.
